items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to the authority of the New
York black car operators' injury compensation fund, inc.
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6239

SPONSOR: SAVINO
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the
authority of the New York black car operators' injury compensation fund,
inc.

 
PURPOSE OR IDEA OF GENERAL BILL:

This legislation makes a technical change to clarify the authority of
the Workers' Compensation Board with regard to its ability to provide
benefits consistent with its plan of operation to ensure that 140,000
black car drivers continue to have the availability of vision, telemedi-
cine and other insurance benefits.

In 1999 New York State, with the support of the International Associ-
ation of Machinists, the AFL-CIO, and the owners of black car companies,
created the Black Car Fund to provide workers compensation insurance for
black car operators paid for with a surcharge on every black car ride.
The fund now covers over 140,000 black car operators around the state
including all Uber and Lyft drivers with a surcharge of 2.5%.

In July of 2018, in an effort to control workers' compensation costs
while increasing the safety and wellbeing of black car operators, their
passengers, and the public, the Black Car Fund launched two new cost
containment strategies. The first was to offer drivers in New York State
free vision benefits including a free annual eye exam and access to a
free pair of eyeglasses-when necessary. The second was to offer drivers
access to free telemedicine services as a low-cost alternative to emer-
gency room visits and costly in-person follow-up, when appropriate. As
part of the purchased telemedicine plan drivers may also calla doctor
outside of a work-related injury.

In May of 2019 the New York State Workers' Compensation Board raised
concerns that these two new cost containment programs may not meet a
strict reading of the current law which authorizes The Black Car Fund to
spend money for "securing the payment of workers' compensation" and "any
statutory penalty resulting from the failure to secure such payment."
(WCL section 11). This legislation would make it clear that The Black
Car Fund can spend an amount of money equal to a surcharge of 0.5% for
benefits that do not fall within the strict reading of the law.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

The bill amends Article 6-F, Section 160-ii of the executive law, as
added by chapter 49 of the laws of 1999, to add a new paragraph (5) that
Clarifies that the Black Car Fund has the authority to provide addi-
tional benefits, consistent with its plan of operation. The legislation
sets the amount of money the Black Car Fund can spend on benefits other
than workers' compensation payments and penalties related thereto at an
amount equal to a surcharge of 0.5%.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

A strict reading of the Workers' Compensation Law could lead the Work-
ers' Compensation Board to shut down any additional benefits program The
Black Car Fund offers even if its intent is to reduce workers' compen-
sation claims, increase driver safety, or protect the public.

The vision and telemedicine programs have proven to be very popular
among drivers with over 14,000 drivers signing up for services in the
first 10 months and 250 new drivers signing up every week. Since 1999
the Machinists have created an affiliate, the Independent Drivers Guild
(IDG), which has also added additional benefits to the package for driv-
ers including a dental discount and prescription drug discount program.
It is too soon to know what impact all of these programs will have on
the cost of workers' compensation claims, but the impact on drivers and
their families is already clear. The Black Car Fund needs the freedom to
continue to experiment with improvements to their services without being
constrained by the narrowest reading of the law.

Recent reports in the media have highlighted the difficult lives drivers
and their families lead. New York has always taken a lead in protecting
these drivers by being the only place in the United States that offers
them workers' compensation insurance, vision and telemedicine coverage,
and, in New York City, a guaranteed minimum wage. This bill prevents the
rolling back of some of these achievements at a time when drivers are in
desperate need of help, while keeping a cap on the cost to consumers.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018 Session - New Legislation

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 77 Chapter 730
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 6239-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to the authority of
        the New York black car  operators'  injury  compensation  funds,
        inc."
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would clarify the authority of the New York Black Car Opera-
tors'  Injury  Compensation  Fund,  Inc.  ("BCF")  to provide additional
health benefits to black car operators who are BCF members. The BCF  was
created to provide workers' compensation coverage to black car operators
in  New York State. The workers' compensation benefits are paid for by a
surcharge on every black car ride. This bill would allow 0.5 percent  of
the existing surcharge to pay for these benefits.

  Since  the  BCF  may  not  require  0.5 percent of the surcharge to be
designated for these benefits, the Executive has  secured  an  agreement
with  the  Legislature to grant the BCF the option to use up to, but not
to exceed, 0.5 percent of the surcharge for this purpose. This agreement
would also establish a timeline for the Executive and the Legislature to
review and assess the BCF's implementation of this bill by  providing  a
sunset  three  years after the date this bill becomes law. Therefore, on
the basis of this agreement, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Relates to the authority of the New York black car operators' injury compensation fund, inc. to provide additional benefits, consistent with its plan of operation, for all black car operators.
